purpose: Primary evidence boundaries for per-instance grinder calibration
rule: Do not transfer a dial, burr-gap, PSD or shot-response curve between grinder instances, burr sets, coffees or brew methods without matched measurements.

sources.title: The effect of bean origin and temperature on grinding roasted coffee
sources.method: Laser diffraction; fixed dial 2.7; four origins; controlled bean temperatures; triplicate/duplicate runs
sources.measuredClaim: PSD was independent of origin and processing method under the tested conditions; cold grinding narrowed PSD and reduced mean size.
sources.notAClaim: Does not establish a universal bean-origin effect or a dial-to-gap curve.

sources.title: Systematically Improving Espresso: Insights from Mathematical Modeling and Experiment
sources.method: PSD measurements across EK43 settings and espresso extraction on a San Remo Opera using 20 g baskets
sources.measuredClaim: Coarse/boulder response and fines response differ; measured extraction yield peaks rather than increasing indefinitely with finer grinding.
sources.notAClaim: Does not provide a pitch or coordinate conversion for plugin home grinders.
sources.license: Accepted manuscript is identified as CC BY-NC-ND; verify asset reuse

sources.title: The role of fines in espresso extraction dynamics
sources.authors: Samo Smrke, Andre Eiermann and Chahan Yeretzian
sources.method: Costa Rica coffee; Vertical 63 burr-spacing settings 160, 170, 180, 190, 210, 250; Camsizer X2; 20 g in / 40 g out at 9 bar on Victoria Arduino Black Eagle; three replicates
sources.measuredClaim: Increasing fines reduced bed permeability, flow rate and increased extraction time; the Vertical 63 scale is calibrated to burr spacing in micrometres.
sources.notAClaim: Does not transfer its burr-spacing-to-shot relationship to DF64, DF54 or other burrs.
